extraction.name: TOFU
extraction.description: TOFU is a benchmark for fictitious unlearning in large language models. It provides a dataset of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each consisting of 20 question-answer pairs, along with forget/retain splits for evaluating unlearning methods and metrics for forget quality and model utility.
extraction.creator: Pratyush Maini; Zhili Feng; Avi Schwarzschild; Zachary C. Lipton; J. Zico Kolter
extraction.citeAs: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, and J. Zico Kolter. TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv:2401.06121, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was curated as fictitious author biographies synthesized by GPT-4 by prompting it with predefined author attributes and asking it to generate 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author. To seed names for book titles, the authors randomly selected keywords from two books from each genre from the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection; Manual Human Curator; Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Synthetic author biographies and question-answer pairs generated by GPT-4 from predefined seed attributes such as birthplace, gender, birth year, genre, awards, parents’ professions, and book-title seeds; book-title seeds were drawn from the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset is composed of fictitious author biographies synthesized by GPT-4 by prompting it with predefined attributes such as birthplace, gender, birth year, genre, awards, parents’ professions, and book-title seeds, and asking it to generate 20 question-answer pairs for each fictitious author; paraphrased answers and five factually incorrect perturbations were also generated with GPT-4 for evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper manually inspected generated biographies to assess diversity and compared word-frequency distributions between an initial raw dataset and the final seeded-prompt dataset; no human label aggregation procedure is described.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: These frequency plots indicate that seeding GPT-4 with author attributes is critical, otherwise, the model is biased toward certain words like ‘tides’, ‘shadows’, and others.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark task is about unlearning information that was learned only during finetuning and not pretraining; the framework considers entity level forgetting and leaves instance level unlearning for future work; the framework is missing a way to think about alignment to human values, which the authors call behavior level unlearning; the benchmark specifically targets measuring the efficacy of an unlearning algorithm and provides the forget sets exactly, rather than addressing how to find a forget set in real-world settings; the current benchmark provides a retain set a priori even though finding an exact retain set is difficult; the purview of TOFU leaves out in-context unlearning; the forget quality measure is only an approximation of indistinguishability and does not fully capture approximate unlearning; the scope of unlearning methods benchmarked is limited to popular but simple algorithms; the authors only consider unlearning algorithms whose work varies linearly with the size of the forget set
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Large language models trained on massive corpora of data from the web can memorize and reproduce sensitive or private data raising both legal and ethical concerns; they can breach individual privacy, either by regurgitating exact details like social security numbers or simply answering questions about people mentioned on the web who would rather not have their information served to others through LLMs; unlearning provides a way to protect private data after training; the work is motivated by regulations around the Right to be Forgotten and aims to help imbue AI systems with the privacy that is critical for safe, and in some places legal, deployment.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper discusses sensitive or private data in LLM training data, including exact details like social security numbers; however, the TOFU dataset itself is entirely fabricated fictitious author biographies, ensuring that no remnants of it exist in the model’s pretraining phase.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: a benchmark aimed at helping deepen our understanding of unlearning; evaluating the efficacy of unlearning methods for LLMs; studying privacy-preserving unlearning in a controlled setup simulating the Right to be Forgotten for private individuals; training and evaluating models on fictitious author question answering and forgetting specific subsets of that information
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: This dataset is released as TOFU: Task of Fictitious Unlearning and can be accessed through Hugging Face; TOFU could be updated in the future to include a constraint not to use the original retain set, which would capture this element of the unlearning pipeline.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset is composed entirely of fictitious author biographies synthesized by GPT-4. It is crafted by prompting GPT-4 to generate data about each author based on predefined attributes, and the benchmark includes three different splits: 90-10, 95-5, and 99-1 retain-forget splits.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To reduce confounders from GPT-4 generation, the authors modified the prompt to deterministically seed author attributes such as place/time of birth, gender orientation, genre, parents’ occupations, and words in book titles. For book-title seeds, they randomly selected keywords from two books from each genre in the Goodreads Books dataset to ensure diversity.
